The origin in my view is the first view. Do you not see that the term for fasting (ṣiyām) is abstaining from food and drink, and the origin of ṣiyām is remaining steadfast in abstaining from food? Likewise ṣalāt is only clinging to what Allah has made obligatory, and ṣalāt is among the greatest obligations He has commanded to be clung to. As for al-muṣallī, the horse that comes immediately after the winner (al-sābiq) in a race, it is named from al-ṣalawān without doubt, these being the two sides flanking the horse's tail; it is as though it comes at that place. The poet said, concerning ṣiyām which is remaining steadfast in standing:

خَيْلٌ صِيامٌ وخَيْلٌ غَيْرُ صائِمَةٍ ∗∗∗ تَحْتَ العَجاجِ وخَيْلٌ تَعْلِكُ اللُّجُما
(Horses standing still, and horses not standing still beneath the dust, and horses champing at the bits.)

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإنّا إلَيْهِ راجِعُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 156] — most [say], in His saying "إنّا لِلَّهِ", the alif with tafkhīm (full, heavy articulation) and adhering to the fatḥa. It has also been said — and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs — "إنّا لِلَّهِ" with imāla (inclination) of the alif towards kasra; that occurred in this expression through frequency of use. Some grammarian claimed that the nūn was given kasra; he did not understand what the people said: it is only that the alif is inclined towards kasra. And he claimed that this is like their saying "اَلْحَمْدِ لِلَّهِ" ("praise be to Allah" with kasra on al-ḥamd). This — I mean their saying "إنّا لِلَّهِ" with kasra — is correct, whereas their saying "اَلْحَمْدِ لِلَّهِ" is among the gravest of errors; so how can what is correct by consensus be like what is an error?!

zajjaj:234-234.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكم ويَذَرُونَ أزْواجًا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأنْفُسِهِنَّ أرْبَعَةَ أشْهُرٍ وعَشْرًا﴾: this concerns the woman whose husband has died; she must wait after his death, if she is not pregnant, four months and ten, not marrying during them and not using adornment. The grammarians have given more than one view concerning the khabar (predicate) of ”اَلَّذِينَ“. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: the meaning is "they wait after them", or "after their death". Others among the Basrans said: "their wives wait", and ”أزْواجُهم“ was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech; this is the consensus of the Basrans, and it is correct. The Kufans said — and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ and his doctrine — that when nouns are annexed to something and the reliance in the predication is on the second, the predication is made about the second and the predication about the first is left aside, the predication about the second sufficing in place of the predication about the first. They said: so the meaning is ”وَأزْواجُ الَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ“ ("and the wives of those who die wait"). Al-Farrāʾ recited:
؎لَعَلِّيَ إنْ مالَتْ بِيَ الرِّيحُ مَيْلَةً ∗∗∗ عَلى ابْنِ أبِي ذُبّانَ أنْ يَتَقَدَّما
(Perhaps I — if the wind should sway me once towards Ibn Abī Dhubbān — that he would come forward.)
The meaning is: perhaps Ibn Abī Dhubbān will come forward to me, if the wind sways me once towards him. This view is not permissible: it is not permissible for a noun to be put at the beginning and nothing be said about it, because speech was established only to convey information, and what conveys nothing is not sound. It is also impossible by their own doctrine, because [according to them] a noun is put in the nominative by a noun only when something like it is made the subject or a returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) to it is mentioned; so this is invalid on their own view, since no noun has come that puts it in the nominative, nor has any returning pronoun to it been mentioned. What I hold to be right in this question is that the mention of ”اَلَّذِينَ“ has occurred as the subject (ibtidāʾ), and the mention of the wives has occurred connected with the ṣila (relative clause) of ”اَلَّذِينَ“, so that the pronoun in ”يَتَرَبَّصْنَ“ refers back to the wives as annexed to ”اَلَّذِينَ“, as if you had said ”يَتَرَبَّصُ أزْواجُهم“ ("their wives wait"). Similar to this in speech is your saying ”اَلَّذِي يَمُوتُ ويُخَلِّفُ ابْنَتَيْنِ تَرِثانِ الثُّلُثَيْنِ“ ("he who dies and leaves two daughters — they inherit two-thirds"), the meaning being ”تَرِثُ ابْنَتاهُ الثُّلُثَيْنِ“ ("his two daughters inherit two-thirds").
The meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَعَشْرًا﴾: the days are included in it. Sībawayh held that when you say ”لِخَمْسٍ بَقِينَ“ ("with five [nights] remaining"), the person addressed knows that the days are included with the nights. Others held that the feminine form prevails in this chapter. Al-Farrāʾ reported ”صُمْنا عَشْرًا مِن شَهْرِ رَمَضانَ“ ("we fasted ten of the month of Ramadan"), and fasting is only by day, but the feminine prevails in [counting] nights, by the consensus of the philologists: ”سِرْنا خَمْسًا، بَيْنَ يَوْمٍ ولَيْلَةٍ“ ("we travelled five, days and nights together"). Sībawayh recited:
؎فَطافَتْ ثَلاثًا بَيْنَ يَوْمٍ ولَيْلَةٍ ∗∗∗ يَكُونُ النَّكِيرُ أنْ تَصِيحَ وتَجْأرا
(She circled three, days and nights together, her only protest being to cry out and moan.)
Sībawayh said: this is the chapter of the feminine which is used for both feminine and masculine, the feminine being its origin. He said: you say ”عِنْدِي ثَلاثُ بَطّاتٍ ذُكُورٌ، وثَلاثٌ مِنَ الإبِلِ ذُكُورٌ“ ("I have three ducks, males, and three camels, males"), because you say ”هَذِهِ إبِلٌ“ (feminine); and likewise ”ثَلاثٌ مِنَ الغَنَمِ ذُكُورٌ“. He said: but if you say ”عِنْدِي ثَلاثَةُ ذُكُورٍ مِنَ الإبِلِ“, only the masculine is possible, because you mentioned "males" first and then went on to say "of the camels" after the speech had already proceeded on the masculine. There is no disagreement between the Basran and Kufan grammarians on what we have mentioned of the feminine treatment of these things. If you say ”عِنْدِي خَمْسَةٌ بَيْنَ رَجُلٍ وامْرَأةٍ“ ("I have five, men and women together"), you let the masculine prevail and nothing else.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإذا بَلَغْنَ أجَلَهُنَّ﴾ means: the end of these months and the ten. ﴿فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم فِيما فَعَلْنَ في أنْفُسِهِنَّ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ means: there is no blame on you in leaving them, once this period has ended, to marry and to adorn themselves with an adornment the like of which is not disapproved — this is the meaning of ”بِالمَعْرُوفِ“.

zajjaj:235-235.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم فِيما عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِن خِطْبَةِ النِّساءِ﴾: the meaning is that there is no blame on a man for hinting at marriage to a woman who is in her ʿidda (waiting period). Hinting (taʿrīḍ) is for him to say ”إنِّي فِيكِ لَراغِبٌ“ ("I am indeed desirous of you"), or ”إنْ قَضى اللَّهُ أمْرًا كانَ“ ("if Allah decrees a thing, it will be"), and similar speech. It is not permissible for him to settle the matter of marriage while the woman has not yet come out of her ʿidda. The meaning of ”خِطْبَةٌ“ is like the meaning of ”خَطْبٌ“ (an affair, a proposal); as for ”خُطْبَةٌ“, it is something that has a beginning and an end, like a letter. It is reported from one of the Arabs: ”اَللَّهُمَّ ارْفَعْ عَنّا هَذِهِ الضُّغْطَةَ“ ("O Allah, lift this oppression from us"); ”اَلضُّغْطَةُ“ is a pressing that has a continuous beginning and end. As for the meaning of ﴿أوْ أكْنَنْتُمْ في أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: of anything you conceal one says ”أكْنَنْتُهُ“ and ”كَنَنْتُهُ“, and ”أكْنَنْتُهُ“ is more common for what one conceals; and of what you protect you say ”كَنَنْتُهُ، فَهو مَكْنُونٌ“. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَأنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 49], that is, protected. Each of the two is close to the other.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لا تُواعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا﴾: Abū ʿUbayda said: ”اَلسِّرُّ“ is speaking openly of marriage, and he recited:
؎وَيَحْرُمُ سِرُّ جارَتِهِمْ عَلَيْهِمْ ∗∗∗ ويَأْكُلُ جارُهم أنْفَ القِصاعِ
(The "secret" of their neighbour's wife is forbidden to them, and their neighbour eats the first of the bowls.)
Others said: ”اَلسِّرُّ“ is as it were a euphemism (kināya) for intercourse, just as ”اَلْغائِطُ“ is a euphemism for the place [of relieving oneself]. In my view this view is correct.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكاحِ﴾ means: do not resolve upon the contract of marriage; ”عَلى“ was omitted for lightness, as you say ”ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ الظَّهْرَ والبَطْنَ“ ("Zayd struck the back and the belly"), meaning "on the back and the belly". Sībawayh said that omission in these things is not to be used as a basis for analogy.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتّى يَبْلُغَ الكِتابُ أجَلَهُ﴾ means: until the prescription of the Book reaches its term. It is also possible that ”اَلْكِتابُ“ itself has the meaning of ”اَلْفَرْضُ“ (prescription), so the meaning is: until the prescription reaches its term, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيامُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 183], that is, prescribed for you. ”كُتِبَ“ could only come in the sense of ”فُرِضَ“ because what is written settles in people's minds as something established. The meaning of this prescription which reaches its term is: the days of the ʿidda of the divorced woman and of the woman whose husband has died.

zajjaj:236-236.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم إنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ ما لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾: Allah has made known in this verse that the marriage contract without a dower (mahr) is permissible, and that there is no sin on one who divorces a woman he married without a dower, just as there is no sin on one who divorces a woman he married with a dower. And He commanded that the woman married without a dower be given a gift of provision (mutʿa) if she is divorced before the marriage is consummated. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلى المُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وعَلى المُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ﴾; ”قَدَرُهُ“ and ”قَدْرُهُ“ are both read. They said that the provision may be by various things: by giving the woman a servant, by clothing her, or by giving her what she can spend; whichever of these he does as provision is permissible for him, according to his means.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَتاعًا بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ means: according to what you know to be moderate and within the measure of what is possible. It is possible that ”مَتاعًا بِالمَعْرُوفِ“ is in the accusative on the basis of His saying ”وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ مَتاعًا“ ("and provide for them a provision"); and it is possible that it is accusative by "going out" (al-khurūj, i.e. as a ḥāl) from His saying ”عَلى المُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ مَتاعًا“, that is, ”مُمَتِّعًا مَتاعًا“ ("providing a provision").
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَقًّا عَلى المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ is accusative on the basis of ”حَقَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَقًّا“ ("that is due from them as a due"), just as one says ”حَقَقْتُ عَلَيْهِ القَضاءَ“ and ”أحْقَقْتُهُ“, that is, I made it binding.

zajjaj:237-237.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنِصْفُ ما فَرَضْتُمْ﴾ means: then upon you is half of what you specified. The accusative is permissible: ”فَنِصْفَ ما فَرَضْتُمْ“, meaning ”فَأدُّوا نِصْفَ ما فَرَضْتُمْ“ ("then pay half of what you specified"); but I do not know anyone who read it so, and if no transmission of it is established, do not read it so.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إلا أنْ يَعْفُونَ أوْ يَعْفُوَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكاحِ﴾: the meaning is: unless the women forgo, or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie forgoes — and he is the husband, or the guardian if he is the father. The meaning of the woman's forgoing is that she forgoes the half of the dower that is due to her and leaves it to the husband; or the husband forgoes the [other] half and gives her the whole. The position of ”يَعْفُونَ“ is accusative by ”أنْ“, except that the feminine plural in the imperfect verb is the same in the nominative, accusative and jussive; we have explained that earlier in the book.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأنْ تَعْفُوا أقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوى ولا تَنْسَوُا الفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: the apparent sense of this address is to the men specifically, not the women, but it may be for both parties, because when an address falls upon males and females the masculine prevails, since the first is more established. The better [reading] in His saying ﴿وَلا تَنْسَوُا الفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ is with ḍamma; ”وَلا تَنْسَوْا اَلْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكم“ is also permissible, and we have explained the reason for it.

zajjaj:119-119.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْناكَ بِالحَقِّ بَشِيرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾. "بَشِيرًا" and "نَذِيرًا" are accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning of "بَشِيرًا" is: giving the believers good tidings of the reward that is theirs, and [نَذِيرًا:] he warns the opponents of the punishment prepared for them.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تُسْألُ عَنْ أصْحابِ الجَحِيمِ﴾. It is also read "وَلا تَسْألُ". The nominative (rafʿ) in both readings is from two angles. One of them is that "وَلا تُسْألُ" is a new beginning (istiʾnāf), as if it were said: "and you are not asked about the companions of Hellfire", as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَإنَّما عَلَيْكَ البَلاغُ وعَلَيْنا الحِسابُ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 40]. It may also take the nominative as a ḥāl, so that the meaning is: "We sent you not asking about the companions of Hellfire". It is also permissible: "وَلا تَسْألْ عَنْ أصْحابِ الجَحِيمِ", and it has been read so; then it is jussive by "لا". There are two views on it, according to what the language requires: that Allah commanded him to leave off asking; or that the prohibition is only in the wording, while the meaning is to magnify the punishment prepared for them — as when someone says to you, about a person whom you yourself know must be in either a fine state or an ugly state, "لا تَسْألْ عَنْ فُلانٍ" (don't ask about so-and-so), i.e. he has come to more than you could want. One says: "سَألْتُهُ، أسْألُهُ، مَسْألَةً، وسُؤالًا" (I asked him). Maṣdars (verbal nouns) on the pattern "فُعالٌ" are rare outside sounds and diseases. As for sounds, like "اَلدُّعاءُ" (calling), "اَلْبُكاءُ" (weeping) and "اَلصُّراخُ" (screaming); as for diseases, like "اَلزُّكامُ" (catarrh), "اَلسُّعالُ" (cough), and the like. It occurred in al-suʾāl only because asking is never without sound.

zajjaj:120-120.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنْ تَرْضى عَنْكَ اليَهُودُ ولا النَّصارى﴾. We have explained the meaning of "اَلْيَهُودُ" and "اَلنَّصارى". As for "تَرْضى", one says of its maṣdar (verbal noun): "رَضِيَ، يَرْضى، رِضًا، ومَرْضاةً، ورِضْوانًا، ورُضْوانًا". It is transmitted from ʿĀṣim that in every occurrence of "رِضْوانٌ" in the Qurʾān [he read] both forms: what Abū ʿAmr transmits from him is "رِضْوانٌ" with kasra, and what Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh transmits is "رُضْوانٌ". Maṣdars come on the patterns "فِعْلانٌ" and "فُعْلانٌ". As for "فِعْلانٌ", it is your saying "عَرَفْتُهُ عِرْفانًا" and "حَسِبْتُهُ حُسْبانًا"; as for "فُعْلانٌ", it is like your saying: "غُفْرانَكَ، لا كُفْرانَكَ" (Your forgiveness, not ingratitude to You). [Translator's note: «حُسْبانًا» as printed has the pattern فُعْلان, though cited under فِعْلان.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتّى تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ﴾. "تَتَّبِعَ" is accusative by "حَتّى". Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and everyone whose knowledge is relied upon say that what puts the verb after "حَتّى" in the accusative is "أنْ", except that it does not appear with "حَتّى". Their proof that "حَتّى" does not itself make [the verb] accusative is that "حَتّى" is, by consensus, a particle that puts [nouns] in the genitive. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَلامٌ هي حَتّى مَطْلَعِ الفَجْرِ﴾ [al-Qadr: 5], so "مَطْلَعِ" is genitive by "حَتّى". We do not know in Arabic that what governs a noun governs a verb, nor that what puts a noun in the genitive puts a verb in the accusative; so it is clear that "حَتّى" is not what makes the accusative. Similarly, when you say "جاءَ زَيْدٌ لِيَضْرِبَكَ" (Zayd came to hit you), the meaning is "جاءَ زَيْدٌ لِأنْ يَضْرِبَكَ", because the lām puts nouns in the genitive and does not put verbs in the accusative. Likewise "ما كانَ زَيْدٌ لِيَضْرِبَكَ" (Zayd would not hit you): the lām is a genitive-governing particle, and what puts "يَضْرِبَكَ" in the accusative is the concealed (muḍmar) "أنْ"; it is not permitted to make it appear with this lām. It is not permitted only because it is an answer to something that comes with the verb and is a single particle: someone says "سَيَضْرِبُكَ" (he will hit you) and "سَوْفَ يَضْرِبُكَ", so the answer in the negative was made with a single particle, just as in the affirmative it was with a single thing. "مِلَّتَهم" is accusative by "تَتَّبِعَ". The meaning of "مِلَّتَهم" in the language is: their way of life and their path. From this is "اَلْمَلَّةُ", i.e. the place in which one bakes bread [in hot ashes], because it leaves its mark in its place as [feet] leave a mark on a path. In the speech of the Arabs, when the wording agrees, most of it is derived one part from another, each part taking hold of the necks of the others.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ هُدى اللَّهِ هو الهُدى﴾, i.e. the path to which He called and guided is the way, i.e. the way of truth.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أهْواءَهُمْ﴾. He used the plural and did not say "هَواهم" only because nothing from him would satisfy all the groups who opposed the Prophet ﷺ except following their [various] desires. "هَوًى" is pluralised as "أهْواءُ", as one says "جَمَلٌ" and "أجْمالٌ" (camels), and "قَتَبٌ" and "أقْتابٌ" (saddles).

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن ولِيٍّ ولا نَصِيرٍ﴾. The genitive in "نَصِيرٍ" is the reading agreed upon; if it were read "وَلا نَصِيرٌ" in the nominative, it would be permissible, because the meaning of "مِن ولِيٍّ" is: "ما لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ ولِيٌّ ولا نَصِيرٌ" (you have no protector nor helper against Allah). The meaning of the verse is that the disbelievers used to ask the Prophet ﷺ for a truce, and made a show that if he made a truce with them and gave them respite they would accept Islam. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that they would never be pleased with him until he followed their religion; so Allah forbade him and admonished him against inclining to anything of what they called to.

zajjaj:121-121.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known to him and to all people that whoever among them was not obstinate, nor envious, nor seeking leadership, recited the Torah as it was sent down, found mentioned in it that the Prophet ﷺ is true, and believed in him. So He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلاوَتِهِ أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾, meaning that those who recited the Torah according to its reality — those believe in the Prophet ﷺ. In this is proof that the others deny what they know to be true, because these were among the scholars of the Jews; likewise those who believed among the scholars of the Christians, of those who recited their books. "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is "يَتْلُونَهُ". If you wish, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is "يَتْلُونَهُ" and "أُولَئِكَ" together, so that the mubtadaʾ has two predicates, as you say: "هَذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ" (this is sweet-sour).

zajjaj:122-122.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا﴾. "يا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ" is accusative because it is a vocative in a genitive construct (iḍāfa), and the base of the vocative is the accusative. Do you not see that when you say "يا بَنِي زَيْدٍ" (O sons of Zayd) and someone asks you "What did you do?", you say "نادَيْتُ بَنِي زَيْدٍ" (I called the sons of Zayd)? It is impossible for you to tell him other than what you did. We have explained this before more fully than this. "إسْرائِيلُ" is a diptote (does not take tanwīn), and we have explained it in its place, along with the dialectal forms it has.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكم وأنِّي فَضَّلْتُكم عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾. The position of "أنَّ" is accusative, as if He said: "Remember that I favoured you over the worlds". The proof from the Qurʾān that they were favoured is the saying of Moses ﷺ, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم إذْ جَعَلَ فِيكم أنْبِياءَ وجَعَلَكم مُلُوكًا وآتاكم ما لَمْ يُؤْتِ أحَدًا مِنَ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 20].

zajjaj:123-123.t: The interpretation of their being favoured in this verse is the kingship they were given, that there were prophets among them, that they were given the knowledge of the Torah, and that in the matter of Jesus and Muhammad — may Allah bless them both and grant them peace — they did not need any sign beyond the knowledge of it that they already had. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reminded them of what they knew and admonished them, saying: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا ولا يُقْبَلُ مِنها عَدْلٌ ولا تَنْفَعُها شَفاعَةٌ﴾. Al-ʿadl is ransom. It was said to them "وَلا تَنْفَعُها شَفاعَةٌ" because they relied on being the sons of Allah's prophets and on [those prophets] interceding for them; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made them despair of that and told them that whoever does not follow Muhammad ﷺ, nothing will save him from the punishment of Allah, and he is a disbeliever.

zajjaj:201-201.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنا آتِنا في الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً وفي الآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وقِنا عَذابَ النّارِ﴾. These are the believers, who ask for a share in this world and the Hereafter. The origin of ”قِنا“ is ”أوْقِينا“, but the wāw dropped, just as it dropped from ”يَقِي“, since the origin is ”يَوْقِي“: the wāw dropped because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra. The connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) dropped because it was no longer needed, since it had been brought in only because the wāw was vowelless; so when the wāw is dropped the speaker has no need of it. The yāʾ dropped for the waqf (indeclinable imperative form), or for the jussive (jazm) according to the view of the Kufans. The meaning is: "make us protected from the punishment of the Fire".

zajjaj:202-202.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم نَصِيبٌ مِمّا كَسَبُوا﴾, i.e. their supplication is answered, because their earning here, which is mentioned, is the supplication. Allah has guaranteed an answer to the supplication of whoever calls upon Him if he is a believer, because He has informed us that He causes the deeds of the unbelievers to go astray and renders them void, and their supplication is among their deeds.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واللَّهُ سَرِيعُ الحِسابِ﴾. The meaning is that He already knows what is in favour of the one being reckoned and what is against him before He makes him stand for his reckoning; so the benefit of the reckoning is the knowledge of its reality. It has been said in some of the exegesis: the reckoning of the servant is quicker than the blink of an eye; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:203-203.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ في أيّامٍ مَعْدُوداتٍ﴾. They said: they are the days of Tashrīq. ”مَعْدُوداتٍ“ is often used in the language for something few. Every number, whether small or large, is counted (maʿdūd), but ”مَعْدُوداتٍ“ points more strongly to fewness, because every small number is pluralised with alif and tāʾ, such as ”دُرَيْهِماتٌ“ and ”جَماعاتٌ“. Yet it is permissible — and it is good and frequent — for the alif and tāʾ to occur for a large number. It is reported that the one who said the following was faulted for it:
؎لَنا الجَفَناتُ الغُرُّ يَلْمَعْنَ بِالضُّحى ∗∗∗ وأسْيافُنا يَقْطُرْنَ مِن نَجْدَةٍ دَما
(Ours are the gleaming bowls that shine in the forenoon, and our swords drip blood from valour.)
It was said to him: why did you make the bowls few, and not say ”اَلْجِفانُ“? This report is, in my view, fabricated, because the alif and tāʾ can come for a large number. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّ المُسْلِمِينَ والمُسْلِماتِ والمُؤْمِنِينَ والمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 35], and He said: ”في جَنّاتٍ“, and He said: ﴿فِي الغُرُفاتِ آمِنُونَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 37]; and the Muslims are not in a few gardens. But when the small number in a plural is specified by alif and tāʾ, the alif and tāʾ point more strongly to it, because it comes next after the dual: you say ”حَمّامٌ“, ”حَمّامانِ“ and ”حَمّاماتٌ“, so it is conveyed with the tāʾ of the singular; thus this points more strongly to the small number, yet it is permissible and good that the large number be meant by it, with the evident meaning indicating what is intended — just as your saying ”جَمْعٌ“ indicates both a small and a large number.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ في يَوْمَيْنِ﴾, i.e. whoever departs within two days, ﴿فَلا إثْمَ عَلَيْهِ لِمَنِ اتَّقى﴾. It is said: for whoever guards against killing game; and they said: for whoever guards against negligence in any of the limits of the Hajj, latitude is given him in hastening his departure.

zajjaj:204-204.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾. The position of ”مَن“ is nominative in two ways: as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the governing element in ”مِن“; we have already explained this topic. It is narrated that a man from Thaqīf used to please the Prophet ﷺ with his speech, displaying to him a fair manner contrary to what was in his heart.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلى ما في قَلْبِهِ﴾. If you said ”وَيَشْهَدُ اللَّهُ عَلى ما في قَلْبِهِ“, it would be permissible, if it has been recited so; and the meaning in it is that Allah knows what he conceals. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed the Prophet ﷺ of the reality of this hypocrite's affair, and said: ﴿وَهُوَ ألَدُّ الخِصامِ﴾. The meaning of ”خَصْمٌ ألَدُّ“ in the language is: one fierce in dispute and argument. Its derivation is from ”لُدَيْدَيِ العُنُقِ“, which are the two sides of the neck. Its interpretation is that whichever direction his opponent takes — right or left — among the avenues of dispute, he overcomes him in it. One says ”رَجُلٌ ألَدُّ“, ”اِمْرَأةٌ لَدّاءُ“ and ”قَوْمٌ لُدٌّ“, and ”قَدْ لَدَدْتُ فُلانًا، ألَدُّهُ“ when I have argued with him and overcome him. ”خِصامٌ“ is the plural of ”خَصْمٍ“, because faʿl, when it is an adjective, is pluralised on fiʿāl, as in ”صَعْبٌ“ / ”صِعابٌ“ and ”خَدْلٌ“ / ”خِدالٌ“. Likewise, if you make ”خَصْمًا“ an adjective, it is pluralised, for both the smaller and the larger number, on fuʿūl and fiʿāl together: one says ”خَصْمٌ“, ”خِصامٌ“ and ”خُصُومٌ“. If it is a noun, then fiʿāl in it is for the larger number, as in ”فَرْخٌ“ with ”أفْراخٌ“ for the smaller number and ”فِراخٌ“ and ”فُرُوخٌ“ for what exceeds ten.

zajjaj:205-205.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذا تَوَلّى سَعى في الأرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيها ويُهْلِكَ الحَرْثَ والنَّسْلَ﴾. ”لِيُفْسِدَ“ is accusative by an implied ”أنْ“; the meaning is: لِأنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيها (in order that he may cause corruption in it) «[Translator's note: the text as vocalised has يُفْسِدُ with ḍamma here; after أنْ one expects يُفْسِدَ.]». ”وَيُهْلِكَ“ is conjoined onto ”يُفْسِدَ“. It may also be that ”يُهْلِكُ الحَرْثَ والنَّسْلَ“ is resumptive (istiʾnāf), i.e. ”وَهو يُهْلِكُ الحَرْثَ والنَّسْلَ“ (and he destroys tillage and offspring), i.e. he is intent on that. They said regarding the tillage (ḥarth) and the offspring (nasl): the ḥarth is the women and the nasl is the children. This is not objectionable, because a woman is called ”حَرْثًا“: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿نِساؤُكم حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 223]. The origin of this is only in crops and everything that is "tilled" (ḥuritha), and that from which a child comes is likened to it. They also said regarding the ḥarth: it is the crops as you know them, because when he causes corruption in the land he nullifies the business of agriculture through his corruption and his stirring up of strife.

zajjaj:207-207.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ﴾. The authorities on the language said: ”يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ“ means he sells himself; and the meaning of his selling himself is his giving it up in striving (jihād) in the way of Allah. The poet said, regarding ”شَرَيْتُ“ in the sense of ”بِعْتُ“ (I sold):
؎وَشَرَيْتُ بُرْدًا لَيْتَنِي ∗∗∗ مِن بَعْدِ بُرْدٍ كُنْتُ هامَةْ
(I sold Burd — would that, after Burd, I had been a dead man's owl.)
The authorities on exegesis said: this was a man called Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān. The polytheists wanted to make him and a group with him abandon Islam, and they killed some of the group who were with him. Ṣuhayb said to them: "I am an old man; if I am against you I will not harm you, and if I am with you I will not benefit you. So leave me to what I follow, and take my wealth." They accepted his wealth from him, and he came to Medina. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, met him and said to him: "The sale has profited, O Ṣuhayb." He answered him: "And yours too — may your sale profit, O Abū Bakr," and recited the verse to him.
”اِبْتِغاءَ مَرْضاةِ اللَّهِ“ is accusative in the sense of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: he sells it for the seeking of Allah's good pleasure.

zajjaj:158-158.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الصَّفا والمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ — "اَلصَّفا" in the language is hard, solid stone that grows nothing. It is a plural; its singular is "صَفاةٌ", and [the plural] "صَفًا", like "حَصاةٍ" and "حَصًى" (pebble, pebbles). "اَلْمَرْوَةُ" and "اَلْمَرْوُ" are soft stones. These two places are among the shaʿāʾir (sacred symbols) of Allah, that is, among the landmarks of His places of worship. The singular of shaʿāʾir is "شَعِيرَةٌ"; the shaʿāʾir are every place of standing, or of running, and of slaughter. Every landmark of that by which worship is performed was called "شَعائِرُ" only because their saying "شَعَرْتُ بِهِ" means "I knew it"; for this reason the landmarks that are places of worship were called "شَعائِرَ".

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمَن حَجَّ البَيْتَ أوِ اعْتَمَرَ فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِ أنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِما﴾ — the Muslims had only avoided circuiting between the two because idols had been set up between them before Islam. So it was said: the setting-up of idols between them before Islam does not necessitate avoiding them, because the Sacred House and the sacred sites were purified by Islam of idols and other things. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that these two are among His shaʿāʾir, and that there is no blame in circuiting between them, and that whoever does that voluntarily — Allah is Appreciative, Knowing. Appreciation (shukr) from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is recompense and fine praise. Ḥajj and ʿumra can be obligatory or voluntary. Circuiting the House runs in the manner of prayer, except that the House is circuited by the pilgrim on ḥajj and the one performing ʿumra, and by one who is neither on ḥajj nor ʿumra. The meaning of their saying "حَجَجْتُ" in the language is: I aimed for; everyone who aims for something has "ḥajj-ed" it, and likewise everyone who aims for something has "iʿtamara-d" it. The poet said:

يَحُجُّ مَأْمُومَةً في قَعْرِها لَجَفٌ ∗∗∗ فاسْتُ الطَّبِيبِ قَذاها كالمَغارِيدِ
(He aims at [i.e. probes] a deep head-wound with a hollow at its bottom… «[Translator's note: the second hemistich is printed in a corrupt form in the source; it describes the physician's probe and the wound's debris, likened to "maghārīd" (a kind of truffle)]»)

And the poet said, regarding his saying "اِعْتَمَرَ", that is, aimed for:

لَقَدْ سَما ابْنُ مُعَمَّرٍ حِينَ اعْتَمَرْ ∗∗∗ مَغْزًى بَعِيدًا مِن بَعِيدٍ وضَبَرْ
(Ibn Muʿammar rose high when he aimed for a distant goal of raiding from afar, and gathered himself [for the leap].)

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِ أنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِما﴾, that is: there is no sin upon him. "اَلْجُناحُ" is taken from "جَنَحَ", when one inclines and deviates from the straight course; its origin is from "جَناحُ الطّائِرِ" (the bird's wing). ﴿أنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِما﴾ has more than one form: "أنْ يَطَّوَّفَ", "أنْ يُطَوِّفَ" and "أنْ يَطُوفَ بِهِما" are permissible. Whoever reads "أنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِما" intends "أنْ يَتَطَوَّفَ", the tāʾ being assimilated (udghimat) into the ṭāʾ because of the nearness of the two points of articulation. Whoever reads "أنْ يُطَوِّفَ بِهِما", it is from "طَوَّفَ", when one circuits much.

In His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا﴾ there are two forms. If you wish you say "وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا" in the wording of the past, its meaning being future, because the speech is a condition and requital (sharṭ wa-jazāʾ), so the wording of the past in it reverts to the meaning of the future. Whoever reads "يَطَّوَّعْ", the origin is "يَتَطَوَّعْ", the tāʾ being assimilated into the ṭāʾ; and you do not assimilate one letter into another without converting it to the sound of the letter it is assimilated into.

zajjaj:159-159.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ ما أنْـزَلْنا مِنَ البَيِّناتِ والهُدى﴾ — this is a report about the scholars of the Jews who concealed what they knew of the soundness of the Prophet's ﷺ affair. His saying: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ ما بَيَّنّاهُ لِلنّاسِ في الكِتابِ﴾ — by it He means the Qurʾān. Concerning the meaning of "وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللّاعِنُونَ" there is more than one view. As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "اَللّاعِنُونَ" (the cursers) are everything on earth except the two weighty ones (al-thaqalān, i.e. humans and jinn). It is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: "اَللّاعِنُونَ" are two people who, when they curse each other, the curse attaches to whichever of them deserves it; and if neither of them deserves it, it returns upon the Jews. And it was said: "اَللّاعِنُونَ" are the believers; everyone who believes in Allah, of humans, jinn and angels, are the cursers of the Jews and of all the disbelievers. This is what has been narrated concerning His saying "اَللّاعِنُونَ", and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best.

zajjaj:160-160.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا وأصْلَحُوا وبَيَّنُوا﴾ — "الَّذِينَ" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as an exception (istithnāʾ). The meaning is that whoever of them repents after this, and it becomes clear [to him] that what the Prophet ﷺ brought is true, Allah accepts his repentance. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He accepts repentance, shows mercy, and forgives the sin beyond which there is no limit.

zajjaj:161-161.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وماتُوا وهم كُفّارٌ﴾ — meaning: they did not repent of their disbelief before their death; upon those is the curse of Allah. The curse (laʿna) is Allah's banishing [them], and His banishing is His punishment.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والمَلائِكَةِ والنّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ﴾ — the meaning is: the curse of the angels and the curse of all people.

If someone says: how do all the people curse him, when the people of his own religion do not curse him? It is said to him: they curse him in the Hereafter, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكم بِبَعْضٍ ويَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 25].

Al-Ḥasan read: "أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ والمَلائِكَةُ والنّاسُ أجْمَعِينَ" (with the nominative), and that is good in Arabic, except that I dislike it because it differs from the Muṣḥaf. In reading, only the Sunna (established practice) should be adhered to, and adherence to the Sunna in it is also stronger in the view of the people of Arabic, because consensus in reading only falls upon what is good and of the highest standard. The nominative of "اَلْمَلائِكَةِ" in al-Ḥasan's reading is on the interpretation: "those, their recompense is that Allah and the angels have cursed them"; so he conjoined the angels to the grammatical position (mawḍiʿ al-iʿrāb) of "اَللَّهِ" in the interpretation. On this basis one may say: "عَجِبْتُ مِن ضَرْبِ زَيْدٍ وعَمْرٌو، ومِن قِيامِكَ وأخُوكَ" ("I marvelled at Zayd's and ʿAmr's striking, and at your and your brother's standing"), the meaning being: "I marvelled that Zayd and ʿAmr struck, and that you and your brother stood". The meaning of "خالِدِينَ فِيها" is: in the curse, and their abiding in it is abiding in the punishment.

zajjaj:163-163.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإلَهُكم إلَهٌ واحِدٌ لا إلَهَ إلا هُوَ﴾ — He, Mighty and Majestic, informed of His oneness, then informed of the argument proving that He is one, and said: ﴿إنَّ في خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ والفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي في البَحْرِ بِما يَنْفَعُ النّاسَ وما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِن ماءٍ فَأحْيا بِهِ الأرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها وبَثَّ فِيها مِن كُلِّ دابَّةٍ وتَصْرِيفِ الرِّياحِ والسَّحابِ المُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ لآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 164]. These signs indicate that He is one, Mighty and Majestic. As for the sign in the matter of the sky, it is among the greatest of signs, because it is a roof without pillars. The sign in the earth is great in what is seen of its plains, its mountains and its seas, and what is in it of the ores of gold, silver, lead and iron, the like of which no one is able to produce. Likewise in the turning about (taṣrīf) of the winds: their turning about is that they come from every horizon, being a north wind at one time, a south wind at another, a west wind (dabūr) at another and an east wind (ṣabā) at another, and they come fertilising the clouds. These things, and all that Allah has spread in the earth, indicate that He is one, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإلَهُكم إلَهٌ واحِدٌ﴾; there is no god other than Him, because no one brings the like of these signs except one [God].

zajjaj:282-282.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا تَدايَنْتُمْ بِدَيْنٍ﴾: one says ”دايَنْتُ الرَّجُلَ“ when I have dealt with the man on credit, taking from him and giving to him; and ”تَدايَنّا“ is on [the pattern of] ”دايَنْتُهُ“. The poet said:
؎دايَنْتُ لَيْلى والدُّيُونُ تُقَضّى ∗∗∗ فَمَطَّلَتْ بَعْضًا وأدَّتْ بَعْضًا
(I dealt on credit with Laylā — and debts are to be repaid — so she delayed some and paid some.)
One also says ”دِنْتُ“ and ”أدَّنْتُ“, i.e. I borrowed; and ”أدَنْتُ“ when I lent. The poet said:
؎أدانَ وأنْبَأهُ الأوَّلُو ∗∗∗ نَ أنَّ المُدانَ مَلِيءٌ وفِيُّ
(He lent, the earlier ones having told him that the borrower was wealthy and faithful.)
So the meaning is: when some of you have a debt owed by others until a stated term, write it down. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — commanded the writing of the debt as a safeguard from Him for property — and likewise the taking of witnesses over it — and [as a safeguard] for people against injustice, because when the one who owes the debt has witnesses and proof against him, his soul seldom tempts him with the hope of making it disappear. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — commanded taking witnesses and writing.

Some of the lexicographers said: this is a [point of] good conduct (adab) from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —, not a binding command, just as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَإذا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصْطادُوا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 2] — for it is not obligatory, whenever one leaves the state of iḥrām, that he hunt — and as He said: ﴿فَإذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فانْتَشِرُوا في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 10]. But this differs from what Allah commanded in writing the debt and taking witnesses, because both of these [other verses] are a permission after a prohibition: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكم صَيْدُ البَرِّ ما دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 96], and said: ﴿لا تَقْتُلُوا الصَّيْدَ وأنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 95], then He permitted them hunting when the iḥrām ended. Likewise He said: ﴿إذا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلاةِ مِن يَوْمِ الجُمُعَةِ فاسْعَوْا إلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وذَرُوا البَيْعَ﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 9], then He permitted them, after the prayer was finished, to seek of His bounty and to disperse in the land for whatever they wanted of selling and other things. The verse of the debt is not like that; rather, what granted a dispensation to forgo taking witnesses, according to the view of some, is His saying: ﴿فَإنْ أمِنَ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أمانَتَهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 283]. That is: he writes with truth; he does not write in favour of the creditor anything in excess against the one who owes the debt, nor does he diminish [the debtor's] right — this is justice. «[Translator's note: this last explanation ("he writes with truth … this is justice") evidently glosses ﴿وَلْيَكْتُبْ بَيْنَكم كاتِبٌ بِالعَدْلِ﴾, which the text does not quote here; it is translated in the order in which it stands.]»

The meaning of ﴿وَلا يَأْبَ كاتِبٌ أنْ يَكْتُبَ كَما عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ﴾ is: let him not refuse to write as Allah commanded him, according to the truth. It is also said: "as Allah taught him, so let him write", i.e. just as Allah has favoured him with [the skill of] writing, let him not withhold kindness through his writing. ”أبى، يَأْبى“ is unique in the language; nothing like it has come except ”قَلى، يَقْلى“, and what has come [authentically] is ”أبى، يَأْبى“ alone, [on the pattern] ”فَعَلَ، يَفْعَلُ“. This [pattern] is not known unless the ʿayn or the lām position of the verb is one of the guttural letters, which we have already explained. But the [correct] view on it is that the alif in ”أبى“ resembled the hamza, so ”يَفْعَلُ“ came with fatḥa for this reason. This view is that of Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq; and like it is ”قَلى، يَقْلى“.

The meaning of His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا يَبْخَسْ مِنهُ شَيْئًا﴾ is: let him not diminish anything from it.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَإنْ كانَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أوْ ضَعِيفًا أوْ لا يَسْتَطِيعُ أنْ يُمِلَّ هُوَ﴾: ”اَلسَّفِيهُ“ is the one light of intellect. From this it is said: ”تَسَفَّهَتِ الرِّيحُ الشَّيْءَ“ (the wind tossed the thing) when it moves it, and ”اِسْتَخَفَّتْهُ“ (it made it light). The poet said:
؎مَشَيْنَ كَما اهْتَزَّتْ رِماحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ ∗∗∗ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ
(They walked as spears sway whose tips are tossed by the passing of gentle winds.)
So children, and women who do not discern soundly, are sufahāʾ; the one weak in his intellect is safīh; and the one who is unable to dictate is the inarticulate one (al-ʿayiyy). It is possible that the very ignorant person is safīh like these. The meaning of ﴿فَلْيُمْلِلْ ولِيُّهُ بِالعَدْلِ﴾ is: the one who manages his affairs, because Allah commanded that we not give the sufahāʾ [their] property, and commanded that it be managed on their behalf, saying: ﴿وارْزُقُوهم فِيها واكْسُوهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 5]. So his walī is the one who stands in his place in [managing] his property, as he would if he were discerning. Some said: [it means] the owner of the debt (walī al-dayn); but this is far-fetched — how could the claimant's word be accepted? And what need would we have of writing and taking witnesses if the word were his word?

﴿واسْتَشْهِدُوا شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِجالِكُمْ﴾: the meaning of ”رِجالِكم“ is: from the people of your religion.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَرَجُلٌ وامْرَأتانِ مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ﴾, i.e. then the one who testifies — if there are not two men — is a man and two women. The meaning of ”مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ“ is: from those whose conduct you approve. By this saying He indicated that among witnesses there are some who ought not to be approved.

﴿أنْ تَضِلَّ إحْداهُما فَتُذَكِّرَ إحْداهُما الأُخْرى﴾: whoever reads ”إنْ“ with kasra, the speech is in the wording and meaning of a conditional (jazāʾ).
The meaning of ”إنْ تَضِلَّ“ is: "if one of them forgets, the one who remembers will remind her, so she will remember"; and ”فَتُذَكِّرُ“ is in the nominative with the kasra of ”إنْ“, nothing else. As for whoever read ”أنْ تَضِلَّ فَتُذَكِّرَ“ — and it is the reading of most people — one of the lexicographers held regarding it that the conditional in it has been brought forward, its original place being later. He said: the meaning is: call two women to witness in place of the man, so that the one who remembers may remind the one who forgets, if she forgets; then, when the conditional was brought forward, it became joined to the beginning of the speech, ”أنْ“ was given fatḥa, and its apodosis was referred back to it. Like it is: ”إنِّي لَيُعْجِبُنِي أنْ يَسْألَ السّائِلُ فَيُعْطى“ (it pleases me that the asker asks and is given). He said: the meaning is: what pleases him is only the giving, if the asker asks. And he held that this is a clear view. But I do not know why the conditional, when brought forward — whether in its place or out of its place — should require ”أنْ“ with it to take fatḥa. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the grammarians whose knowledge is trusted mentioned that the meaning is: call two women to witness so that one of them may remind the other, and for the sake of one of them reminding the other. Sībawayh said: if someone says: why then is ”أنْ تَضِلَّ“ permissible, when this was only prepared for the reminding? The answer is that since the cause of the reminding is the going astray (forgetting), it is permissible to mention ”أنْ تَضِلَّ“, because the going astray is the cause that necessitated the reminding. He said: and like it is ”أعْدَدْتُ هَذا الجِذْعَ أنْ يَمِيلَ الحائِطُ، فَأُدَعِّمَهَ“ (I prepared this trunk lest the wall lean, so that I may prop it up): I only prepared it for propping, not for leaning; but the leaning was mentioned because it is the cause of the propping, just as the going astray was mentioned because it is the cause of the reminding. This is the clear [view], if Allah wills.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا يَأْبَ الشُّهَداءُ إذا ما دُعُوا﴾: it is reported from al-Ḥasan that he said: ”﴿وَلا يَأْبَ الشُّهَداءُ إذا ما دُعُوا﴾“ for initiating the testimony, i.e. and let them not refuse when they are called to [take up and] establish it. What al-Ḥasan said is the truth — and Allah knows best — because if witnesses refused to testify, and that were their right, people's rights would perish and their dealings in which they need security would be voided. Someone other than al-Ḥasan said: ”﴿وَلا يَأْبَ الشُّهَداءُ إذا ما دُعُوا﴾“ when there is a testimony upon their necks, [i.e. let them not refuse] to deliver it; but when they are not [yet] witnesses, they have a choice about initiating the testimony: if they wish they testify, and if they wish they refuse. What indicates the emphasis that the witness ought to respond when he is called initially is His saying — Exalted is He —: ﴿وَلا تَسْأمُوا أنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أوْ كَبِيرًا إلى أجَلِهِ﴾, i.e. do not grow weary of writing down what you have been made to witness; they have been commanded this, and this confirms that the matter of testimony at the outset is obligatory and that one ought not to grow weary of it. One says: ”سَئِمْتُ، أسْأمُ، سَآمَةً، وسَأمًا“. The rajaz poet said:
؎لَمّا رَأيْتُ أنَّهُ لا قامَةْ ∗∗∗ وأنَّنِي ساقٍ عَلى السَّآمَةْ
؎نَزَعْتُ نَزْعًا زَعْزَعَ الدِّعامَةْ
(When I saw that there was no pulley-frame, and that I was drawing water despite weariness, I hauled with a pull that shook the supporting post.)

The meaning of ﴿إلا أنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً حاضِرَةً﴾: most readers have the nominative: ”تِجارَةٌ حاضِرَةٌ“, in the sense of ”إلّا أنْ تَقَعَ تِجارَةٌ حاضِرَةٌ“ (unless there occurs a present transaction). Whoever put ”تِجارَةً“ in the accusative — and it is the reading of ʿĀṣim — the meaning is: unless the dealing on credit is a present transaction. The nominative is more common, and it is the reading of the people. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — granted a dispensation to forgo writing what they circulate among themselves, because of how frequently dealings occur in it, and because trading mostly occurs in small things, even if a debt occurs in it. And He emphasised taking witnesses in selling, saying: ﴿وَأشْهِدُوا إذا تَبايَعْتُمْ﴾. We have already explained what it is that granted a dispensation to forgo taking witnesses.

The meaning of ﴿وَلا يُضارَّ كاتِبٌ ولا شَهِيدٌ﴾: they gave two views about it. Some of them said: ”لا يُضارَّ“ is ”لا يُضارِرْ“; the rāʾ was assimilated into the rāʾ and given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the meaning of ”لا يُضارَّ“ is: let the scribe write only with truth, and let the witness testify only with truth. Others said: ”وَلا يُضارَّ كاتِبٌ ولا شَهِيدٌ“: the scribe is not to be summoned while he is occupied, unable to leave his occupation except with harm befalling him; and likewise the witness is not to be summoned when his coming to testify harms him. The first is clearer, because of His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَفْعَلُوا فَإنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ﴾, for "the transgressor" (al-fāsiq) better fits one who is not just and one who distorts the writing than one who calls a witness to testify, or calls a scribe to write, while he is occupied — such a person is not called a fāsiq; rather, the one who lies in testimony and the one who distorts the writing is called ”فاسِقًا“.

zajjaj:283-283.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَرِهانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ﴾: people read ”فَرُهُنٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ“ and ”فَرِهانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ“. As for ”رُهُنٌ“, it is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, and more than one person mentioned regarding it that it was read ”فَرُهُنٌ“ in order to distinguish between rihān in [racing] horses and the plural of ”رَهْنٌ“ in other things. ”رُهُنٌ“ and ”رِهانٌ“ are more frequent in the language. Al-Farrāʾ said: ”رُهُنٌ“ is the plural of ”رِهانٌ“. Someone else said: ”رُهُنٌ“ and ”رَهْنٌ“ are like ”سُقُفٌ“ and ”سَقْفٌ“; [the plural] ”فُعْلٌ“ of ”فَعْلٌ“ is rare, but it is sound and has occurred; in adjectives, however, it is frequent: one says ”فَرَسٌ ورْدٌ“ (a bay horse) and ”خَيْلٌ وُرْدٌ“ (bay horses), and a man ”ثَطٌّ“ (thin-bearded) and ”قَوْمٌ ثُطٌّ“. The reading ”رُهُنٌ“ is more pleasing to me, because it agrees with the Muṣḥaf; and what agrees with the Muṣḥaf, is sound in meaning, and has been read by the readers is the preferred choice. «[Translator's note: the printed Muṣḥaf has ﴿فَرِهانٌ﴾; the author's remark presumably refers to the unpointed consonantal script without alif. Translated as written.]» ”رِهانٌ“ is good and fully [correct]. One says: ”رَهَنْتُ الرَّهْنَ، وأرْهَنْتُهُ“ (I gave the pledge), and ”أرْهَنْتُ“ is the less common of the two. The poet said, regarding ”أرْهَنْتُ“:
؎فَلَمّا خَشِيتُ أظافِيرَهم ∗∗∗ نَجَوْتُ وأرْهَنْتُهم مالِكًا
(When I feared their claws, I escaped and left them Mālik as a pledge.)
And he said — regarding ”رَهَنْتُ“, recited by more than one person —:
؎فَهَلْ مِن كاهِنٍ أوْ ذِي إلَهٍ ∗∗∗ إذا ما حانَ مِن رَبِّي قُفُولُ
؎يُراهِنُنِي فَيَرْهَنُنِي بَنِيهِ ∗∗∗ وأرْهَنُهُ بَنِيَّ بِما أقُولُ
؎لَما يَدْرِي الفَقِيرُ مَتى غِناهُ ∗∗∗ وما يَدْرِي الغَنِيُّ مَتى يُعِيلُ
(Is there any soothsayer or devotee of a god, when my lord's return is due, who would wager with me, pledging me his sons while I pledge him my sons on what I say: the poor man does not know when he will be rich, nor does the rich man know when he will become poor?)

zajjaj:238-238.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حافِظُوا عَلى الصَّلَواتِ والصَّلاةِ الوُسْطى﴾: they said: the middle prayer is ʿAṣr (the afternoon prayer), and this is what most of the narrations say. It has also been said that it is the morning prayer (al-ghadāh), and it has been said that it is Ẓuhr (the noon prayer). Allah has commanded the guarding of all the prayers; but when this wāw comes singling something out, it indicates the excellence of what it singles out, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَن كانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ ومَلائِكَتِهِ ورُسُلِهِ وجِبْرِيلَ ومِيكالَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 98], where the two are mentioned specifically because of their excellence over the angels. Yūnus the grammarian said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ ونَخْلٌ ورُمّانٌ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 68]: He singled out the date-palm and the pomegranate, though fruit had already been mentioned, only because of their excellence over the rest of it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾: ”اَلْقانِتُ“ is the obedient one, and ”اَلْقانِتُ“ is the one who remembers Allah, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أمَّنْ هو قانِتٌ آناءَ اللَّيْلِ ساجِدًا وقائِمًا﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. It has also been said: ”اَلْقانِتُ“ is the worshipper, and they said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَكانَتْ مِنَ القانِتِينَ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 12]: that is, of the worshippers. What is well known in the language and in usage is that ”اَلْقُنُوتُ“ is supplication while standing. The reality of the qānit is that he is the one who stands (al-qāʾim) by the command of Allah; so the one supplicating, when he is standing, is specifically described as ”قانِتٌ“,
because he is remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, while standing on his feet. So the reality of qunūt is worship and supplication to Allah in the state of standing, and it may also apply to all other obedience, because even if it is not standing on the feet, it is "standing by" a thing (i.e. undertaking it) through intention.

zajjaj:239-239.t:
The meaning of ﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجالا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾ is: then pray riding or on foot. ”رِجالٌ“ is the plural of ”راجِلٌ“ (one on foot); ”رِجالٌ“ is like ”صاحِبٌ“ and ”صِحابٌ“. That is: if you are unable to stand qānitīn — that is, worshipping and giving the prayer its full due — because of fear that befalls you, then pray on foot or riding.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإذا أمِنتُمْ فاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَما عَلَّمَكم ما لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ means: when you are safe, stand qānitīn, performing the obligation.

zajjaj:240-240.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَصِيَّةً لأزْواجِهِمْ﴾ and ”وَصِيَّةٌ لِأزْواجِهِمْ“ are both read. Whoever reads the accusative intends ”فَلْيُوصُوا وصِيَّةً لِأزْواجِهِمْ“ ("let them make a bequest for their wives"); and whoever reads the nominative, the meaning is ”فَعَلَيْهِمْ وصِيَّةٌ لِأزْواجِهِمْ“ ("then a bequest for their wives is incumbent upon them"). ﴿مَتاعًا إلى الحَوْلِ غَيْرَ إخْراجٍ﴾ means: provide for them a provision until the year is out, and do not turn them out. This is abrogated by consensus; what precedes it abrogated it, and we have explained it. It has also been said that the verse of inheritance abrogated it. Both of them — I mean what Allah commanded of waiting four months and ten, and the inheritance He assigned to them — have abrogated it.

zajjaj:242-242.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكم آياتِهِ لَعَلَّكم تَعْقِلُونَ﴾: ”آياتِهِ“ means His signs and His indications of what He has made obligatory upon you; that is, with the like of this clarification He makes clear to you what is obligatory upon you and what has been imposed upon you. The meaning of ﴿لَعَلَّكم تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ is a meaning that needs a thorough explanation, because the philologists and exegetes have reported about it only what is apparent. Its reality is that the one who has understanding (al-ʿāqil) here is the one who acts upon what has been made obligatory upon him, because if he understands the obligation and does not act upon it, he is ignorant, not one who has understanding. The reality of understanding (al-ʿaql) is putting upright things into practice once they are known. Do you not see His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّما التَّوْبَةُ عَلى اللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ بِجَهالَةٍ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبٍ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 17]? If these people were ignorant and wholly lacking discernment, the obligation would have lapsed from them, because Allah does not impose obligation on one who has no discernment. They are called ignorant even though they have discernment, because they preferred their desires over what they knew to be the truth.

zajjaj:243-243.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ وهم أُلُوفٌ حَذَرَ المَوْتِ﴾: the meaning of ”ألَمْ تَرَ؟“ is ”ألَمْ تَعْلَمْ؟“ ("do you not know?"), that is: has your knowledge not reached the report of these people? This alif is the alif of tawqīf (bringing to attention), and ”تَرَ“ has its hamza dropped; its original is ”ألَمْ تَرَءْ إلى الَّذِينَ“, and the Arabs agree on dropping the hamza in this. ”حَذَرَ المَوْتِ“ is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is "they went out for fear of death", and when the lām fell away it was put in the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because their going out indicates "fearing death with a fearing". It has been said in the interpretation of the verse that they were eight thousand, who were commanded in the days of the Children of Israel «[Translator's note: the source repeats the word إسْرائِيلَ here: «بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ إسْرائِيلَ».]» to fight the enemy, but they made the excuse that the place to which they had been summoned was afflicted by plague. ﴿فَقالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا﴾ means: so Allah caused them to die. It is said that they were kept dead for eight days and then brought back to life. In the mention of this verse to the Prophet ﷺ there is an argument against the polytheists of the Arabs and against the People of the Book among the Jews and the Christians: he informed the People of the Book of something whose truth they could not reject, while he ﷺ had not read any book. Those to whom he recited knew that he had not read any book and that he was unlettered (ummī), so he could not know these stories except by revelation, since they were not learned from a book. So the polytheists of the Arabs knew that everyone who had read the scriptures confirmed him ﷺ in his report that these things were in their books; and the Arabs among whom he grew up knew likewise that he had never been absent for a time in which he could have been taught the stories and reports of the nations with truth and accuracy. In this verse there is also the sense of urging to jihad, and that death is not averted by fleeing from it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلى النّاسِ﴾ means: He bestowed favour on these people by bringing them back to life after their death, and so showed them an insight beyond which there is nothing further.

zajjaj:244-244.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, following this verse: ﴿وَقاتِلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ means: do not flee from death as these people whose report you have heard fled, for fleeing will not benefit you.
The meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, together with the mention of fighting: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ is: if you speak as those mentioned before spoke, making excuses to flee from death, He hears your words and knows what you intend.

zajjaj:245-245.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾: the meaning of ”اَلْقَرْضُ“ in the language is a bad deed done to someone or a good deed done to someone (al-balāʾ). The Arabs say: ”لَكَ عِنْدِي قَرْضٌ حَسَنٌ، وقَرْضٌ سَيِّئٌ“ ("I owe you a good turn / a bad turn"). Its origin is what a man gives or does in order to be repaid for it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, does not seek a loan out of need, but He tests the reports «[Translator's note: so in the source, «الأخْبارَ»; perhaps a misreading of «الأخْيارَ», "the good people".]»; so the qarḍ is as we have described. Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt said:
؎لا تَخْلِطَنَّ خَبِيثاتٍ بِطَيِّبَةٍ ∗∗∗ واخْلَعْ ثِيابَكَ مِنها وانْجُ عُرْيانا
(Do not mix foul deeds with a good one; strip off your garments of them and escape naked.)
؎كُلُّ امْرِئٍ سَوْفَ يُجْزى قَرْضَهُ حَسَنًا ∗∗∗ أوْ سَيِّئًا أوْ مَدِينًا كالَّذِي دانا
(Every man will be repaid his qarḍ, good or bad, or requited just as he dealt.)
And the poet said:
؎وَإذا جُوزِيتَ قَرْضًا فاجْزِهِ ∗∗∗ إنَّما يَجْزِي الفَتى لَيْسَ الجَمَلْ
(When you are repaid a qarḍ, repay it; it is the true man who repays, not the camel.)
So the meaning of qarḍ is what we have mentioned. Allah made known that whatever is done and spent with the intention of reward, Allah multiplies it many times over. The reading is ”فَيُضاعِفَهُ“, and they read ”فَيُضاعِفُهُ“ — with the accusative and with the nominative. Whoever reads the nominative conjoins it to ”يُقْرِضُ“; and whoever conjoins, reads the accusative as the answer to the interrogative «[Translator's note: so in the source, «ومَن عَطَفَ نَصَبَ»; the sense requires "whoever reads the accusative makes it the answer to the interrogative".]». We have already explained the answer with fāʾ. If ”قَرْضًا“ here were a maṣdar (verbal noun), it would be ”إقْراضًا“; but ”قَرْضًا“ here is a noun for anything for which a reward is sought. As for ”قَرَضْتُهُ، أقْرُضُهُ، قَرْضًا“, it means "I passed it by". The root of ”اَلْقَرْضُ“ in the language is cutting, and ”اَلْقِراضُ“ (partnership in trade) is taken from this; so ”أقْرَضْتُهُ“ means only: I cut off for him a portion for which I will be repaid.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ ويَبْسُطُ﴾: more than one view has been given on this. Some said: it means "He straitens and He makes ample". Some said: "He strips some people of what He had bestowed on them and gives ample to others". It has also been said that the meaning of ”يَقْبِضُ“ is: He takes the charitable gifts and replaces them; and their replacement may be the reward He gives in the Hereafter, and it may be that, together with the reward, He replaces them in this world.

zajjaj:124-124.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذِ ابْتَلى إبْراهِيمَ رَبُّهُ بِكَلِماتٍ فَأتَمَّهُنَّ﴾. The meaning is: remember when his Lord tested Abraham. The meaning of "فَأتَمَّهُنَّ" is: he fulfilled what he was commanded in them. They differed over the "words" (al-kalimāt). Some said: their explanation is that He commanded him five practices concerning the head and five practices concerning the body. Those concerning the head are: parting the hair, trimming the moustache, the tooth-stick (siwāk), rinsing the mouth, and sniffing water into the nose. Those concerning the body are: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, cleansing after relieving oneself (istinjāʾ), clipping the nails and plucking the armpit hair. This is the doctrine of some, and many of the exegetes hold it. Others said: what He tested him with was His commanding him to sacrifice his son, his being thrown into the fire, and the matter of the stars mentioned in the Qurʾān in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلَمّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأى كَوْكَبًا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 76], and what follows the stars of the mention of the moon and the sun. This is the doctrine of some.

Abraham was tested with all of these qualities, and he fulfilled what he was commanded, and did what a believer does — nay, what the righteous, chosen, elect one does. The meaning of "اِبْتَلى" is: tested.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنِّي جاعِلُكَ لِلنّاسِ إمامًا﴾. Al-amm in the language is aiming (qaṣd). You say "أمَمْتُ كَذا وكَذا" when you have aimed for it. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 43], i.e. so aim for. Al-imām is the one who is followed (yuʾtammu bihi), so that his people and his community do as he did, i.e. they aim for what he aims for.

﴿قالَ ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِي قالَ لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظّالِمِينَ﴾. So Allah made known to Abraham that among his offspring there would be wrongdoers. It has been read: "لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظّالِمُونَ", and the meaning in the nominative and the accusative is one, because "attaining" (al-nayl) involves both the covenant and the wrongdoers, except that it is negated of them. The good reading is with "اَلظّالِمِينَ" in the accusative, because that is how it is in the muṣḥaf. That [other] reading is good and eloquent, except that I do not read it, and it should not be read, because it is contrary to the muṣḥaf; and because the meaning is that Abraham, peace be upon him, as it were said: "Make the imamate reach my offspring, and make this covenant reach my offspring", and Allah said: "﴿لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظّالِمِينَ﴾" — so on this [construal] it is also stronger.

zajjaj:125-125.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذْ جَعَلْنا البَيْتَ مَثابَةً لِلنّاسِ وأمْنًا﴾. "مَثابَةً": they return (yathūbūna) to it. "اَلْمَثابُ" and "اَلْمَثابَةُ" are one, and likewise "اَلْمَقامُ" and "اَلْمَقامَةُ". The poet said:

؎وَإنِّي لَقَوّامٌ مَقاوِمَ لَمْ يَكُنْ ∗∗∗ جَرِيرٌ ولا مَوْلى جَرِيرٍ يَقُومُها
(I am one who stands in places of standing in which neither Jarīr nor Jarīr's client could ever stand.)

The singular of "اَلْمَقاوِمُ" is "مَقامٌ". And Zuhayr said:

؎وَفِيهِمْ مَقاماتٌ حِسانٌ وُجُوهُها ∗∗∗ وأنْدِيَةٌ يَنْتابُها القَوْلُ والفِعْلُ
(Among them are assemblies with handsome faces, and gatherings frequented by [fine] word and deed.)

The singular of "اَلْمَقاماتُ" is "مَقامَةٌ". The base form of "مَثابَةً" is "مَثْوَبَةً", but the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the letter before the wāw is the thāʾ], and the wāw followed the vowel and turned into alif. This is a weakening (iʿlāl) by conformity: "مَثابَةً" followed the pattern of "ثابَ", and the base of "ثابَ" is "ثَوَبَ", but the wāw was turned into alif because it is vowelled and the letter before it has fatḥa; there is no disagreement among the grammarians about that. This chapter has some difficulty, but this book of ours comprises the explanation of i'rab and meanings, so they must be treated thoroughly as far as is known. As for the meaning of His saying "وَأمْنًا", it has been said: whoever committed a crime and then entered the Sanctuary (al-ḥaram) would not have the ḥadd (prescribed penalty) carried out on him; but no one would trade with him or speak to him until he was forced to leave it, and then the ḥadd would be carried out on him.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واتَّخِذُوا مِن مَقامِ إبْراهِيمَ مُصَلًّى﴾. It has been read "واتَّخِذُوا" with fatḥa and with kasra: "واتَّخَذُوا" and "واتَّخِذُوا". It is transmitted «that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to the Prophet ﷺ, when they had stopped at the Station of Abraham: Is this not the station of the intimate friend of our Lord? — some said: the station of our father — Shall we not take it as a place of prayer? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿واتَّخِذُوا مِن مَقامِ إبْراهِيمَ مُصَلًّى﴾». So the command, and the reading "واتَّخِذُوا" with kasra, are clearer according to this report. But "واتَّخَذُوا" is not ruled out, because people did take this [as a place of prayer]; so He said: "وَإذْ جَعَلْنا البَيْتَ مَثابَةً... واتَّخَذُوا", conjoining a sentence to a sentence.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَهِدْنا إلى إبْراهِيمَ وإسْماعِيلَ أنْ طَهِّرا بَيْتِيَ لِلطّائِفِينَ والعاكِفِينَ والرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ﴾. The meaning of "purify it" is: keep it from having idols hung on it. Those circumambulating are those who go round the House; al-ʿākifūn are those who stay at it. One says: "قَدْ عَكَفَ، يَعْكُفُ، ويَعْكِفُ عَلى الشَّيْءِ عُكُوفًا", i.e. he stayed constantly at it; from this is people's saying: "فُلانٌ مُعْتَكِفٌ عَلى الحَرامِ" (so-and-so persists in what is forbidden), i.e. stays constantly at it. "اَلرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ" are all the Muslims who pray in it. In "بَيْتِيَ" the best is to give the yāʾ a fatḥa, and if you wish you may make it quiescent. "اَلرُّكَّعِ" is the plural of "راكِعٍ", like "غازٍ" and "غُزًى" (raiders), and "اَلسُّجُودِ" is the plural of "ساجِدٍ", as in your saying "ساجِدٌ" and "سُجُودٌ", and "شاهِدٌ" and "شُهُودٌ" (witnesses).

zajjaj:126-126.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذا بَلَدًا آمِنًا﴾. The meaning is: "And remember when Abraham said...". "آمِنًا" means: possessing security.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وارْزُقْ أهْلَهُ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ مَن آمَنَ مِنهُمْ﴾. "مَن" is accusative, a badal (substitute) from "أهْلَهُ"; the meaning is: provide for those of its people who believe, to the exclusion of others — because Allah, Exalted is He, had made known to him that among his offspring there would be non-believers, by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظّالِمِينَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 124].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَ ومَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلا ثُمَّ أضْطَرُّهُ إلى عَذابِ النّارِ﴾. Most readers read "فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ أضْطَرُّهُ" as a statement. It has also been read "فَأمْتِعْهُ... ثُمَّ اضْطَرَّهُ" as a supplication. The form of supplication is like the form of command — jussive — except that it was considered too grave to call it "a command". So your request to someone above you, like "أعْطِنِي" (give me) and "اِغْفِرْ لِي" (forgive me), is supplication and request, while your request to someone below you is a command, like your saying to your servant: "Do such-and-such." The rāʾ in His saying "ثُمَّ اضْطَرَّهُ" has fatḥa because it is quiescent and the rāʾ before it is quiescent; the base is "ثُمَّ اضْطَرِرْهُ". "ثُمَّ اضْطَرْهُ" is also permissible, but I know of no one who read it.

zajjaj:127-127.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذْ يَرْفَعُ إبْراهِيمُ القَواعِدَ مِنَ البَيْتِ﴾. "اَلْقَواعِدُ": its singular is "قاعِدَةٌ"; it is like "اَلْأساسُ" and "اَلْأُسُّ" (foundation) of a building, except that every qāʿida is [a base] for what is above it. ﴿وَإسْماعِيلُ﴾ is conjoined to "إبْراهِيمُ".

His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا تَقَبَّلْ مِنّا﴾. The meaning is: the two of them say: Our Lord, accept from us. Its like in the Book of Allah is: ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ باسِطُو أيْدِيهِمْ أخْرِجُوا أنْفُسَكُمُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 93], and likewise: ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن كُلِّ بابٍ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 23] ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 24], i.e. they say: "سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم" (peace be upon you).

zajjaj:208-208.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا في السِّلْمِ كافَّةً﴾. ”كافَّةً“ has the sense of totality and comprehensiveness. Its meaning may be ”اُدْخُلُوا جَمِيعًا“ (enter, all of you), or its meaning may be ”اُدْخُلُوا في السِّلْمِ كُلِّهِ“ (enter into the whole of al-silm), i.e. into all of its laws. One says both ”اَلسِّلْمُ“ and ”اَلسَّلْمُ“, and what is meant by it is Islam, and peace. There are three dialectal forms of it: one says ”اَلسِّلْمُ“, ”اَلسَّلَمُ“ and ”اَلسَّلْمُ“; and it has been recited so in: ﴿وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَن ألْقى إلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 94]. The meaning of ”كافَّةً“ in the derivation of the language is: that which restrains (yakuffu) a thing at its end. From this is ”كُفَّةُ القَمِيصِ“: the hem of a shirt is called ”كُفَّةٌ“, and the edge of everything elongated is a ”كُفَّةٌ“, while of everything round one says ”كِفَّةٌ“, as in ”كِفَّةُ المِيزانِ“ (the pan of the scales). It is said that the hem of a garment is called ”كُفَّةُ الثَّوْبِ“ only because it prevents it from unravelling. The origin of ”اَلْكَفُّ“ is prevention; from this the extremity of the arm is called ”كَفٌّ“ (the hand), because by it one keeps (things) off the rest of the body — and it is the palm together with the fingers. From this also it is said ”رَجُلٌ مَكْفُوفٌ“ (a blind man), i.e. his sight has been held back from seeing. So the meaning of the verse is: reach in Islam to where its laws end, and hold back from transgressing its laws; or: enter, all of you, until it is held back from any one who has not entered it «[Translator's note: the phrase عَنْ عَدَدٍ وأحَدٍ is obscure as transmitted; the sense appears to be "so that none is left who has not entered".]». It is said regarding the meaning of the verse that some Jews became Muslim but persisted in holding the Sabbath sacred and in forbidding the eating of camel meat, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded them to enter into all the laws of Islam. Some of the authorities on the language said: it may be that He commanded them — while they were believers — to enter into faith, i.e. to persist in faith and to remain on it in what lies ahead of them, as He said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ والكِتابِ الَّذِي نَـزَّلَ عَلى رَسُولِهِ والكِتابِ الَّذِي أنْـزَلَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 136]. Both views are permissible, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has commanded persistence in Islam, saying: ﴿وَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إلا وأنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 102].
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ﴾, i.e. do not follow in his tracks, because your leaving any of the laws of Islam is following Satan. ”خُطُواتٌ“ is the plural of ”خُطْوَةٌ“, and there are three dialectal forms of it: ”خُطُواتٌ“, ”خُطَواتٌ“ and ”خُطْواتٌ“. We have explained the reason for this plural earlier in the book.

zajjaj:209-209.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإنْ زَلَلْتُمْ مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْكُمُ البَيِّناتُ﴾. One says ”زَلَّ، يَزِلُّ، زَلًّا، وزَلَلًا“, both, and ”مَزَلَّةً“, and ”زَلَّ في الطِّينِ زَلِيلًا“ (he slipped in the mud). The meaning of ”زَلَلْتُمْ“ is: you swerved away from the right course and the laws. ﴿فاعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: the meaning of ”عَزِيزٌ“ is that they cannot thwart Him and nothing thwarts Him; and the meaning of ”حَكِيمٌ“ is: wise in what He created you upon, and in what He has prescribed for you of His religion.

zajjaj:210-210.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا أنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ في ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الغَمامِ والمَلائِكَةُ﴾. The authorities on the language said: its meaning is that Allah comes to them with the punishment and the reckoning He promised them, as He said: ﴿فَأتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 2], i.e. He came to them with His forsaking of them. ”ظُلَلٌ“ is the plural of ”ظُلَّةٌ“. ”اَلْمَلائِكَةُ“ is recited in two ways: with ḍamma and with kasra. Whoever recites ”اَلْمَلائِكَةُ“ in the nominative, the meaning is: "do they wait for anything but that Allah and the angels should come to them?"; and the nominative is the preferred form in recitation according to the authorities on the language. Whoever recites ”والمَلائِكَةِ“, the meaning is: "do they wait for anything but that Allah should come to them in canopies of cloud and canopies of angels?". The meaning of ”وَقُضِيَ الأمْرُ“ is: what they were promised has been settled for them. And the meaning of ﴿وَإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾ and ”تَرْجِعُ الأُمُورُ“ — both are recited — is: "are returned".
If someone says: "Are not matters — now and at every time — returning to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?", the meaning in this is the announcement concerning the matter of the reckoning, the reward and the punishment, i.e. to Him you will come, and He will punish whom He wills and have mercy on whom He wills.

zajjaj:211-211.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَلْ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْناهم مِن آيَةٍ بَيِّنَةٍ﴾. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and the meaning is for him and for all the believers and others. The meaning is that they were given clear signs, whose mention has gone before, and they knew the truth of the Prophet's ﷺ affair, yet they denied it while knowing its reality.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُ﴾: by it in this place He means the proofs of Allah indicating the affair of His Prophet ﷺ; ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾, i.e. severe in punishing.

zajjaj:212-212.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الحَياةُ الدُّنْيا﴾. It («الحَياةُ») is nominative as the one whose agent is not named (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). In ”زُيِّنَ“ the masculine form is permissible; had it been ”زُيِّنَتْ“ it would be correct, and ”زَيَّنَ“ is correct and good, because the femininity of al-ḥayāt is not real (grammatical only), since the meaning of al-ḥayāt and the meaning of al-ʿaysh (living) are one; and also, a separation has been made between the verb and the feminine noun.
Two views have been given on His saying ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الحَياةُ الدُّنْيا﴾. Some of them said: Iblīs made it attractive to them, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has urged renunciation of it and made known that it is the enjoyment of delusion. Some of them said: its meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, created in it pleasing things, and those who disbelieved looked at them as more than their worth. The proof for these people's view is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلنّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَواتِ مِنَ النِّساءِ والبَنِينَ والقَناطِيرِ المُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ والفِضَّةِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 14]. Both are permissible.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾. Some of the polytheists used to mock the Muslims because their state in terms of possessions was meagre; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that those who are God-fearing will be above them on the Day of Resurrection, because the Muslims will be in ʿIlliyyīn and the wicked in Hell. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ أجْرَمُوا كانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 29]. The meaning of ﴿واللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ is: He does not provide for the believer in proportion to his faith, nor provide for the unbeliever in proportion to his unbelief. This is the meaning of ”بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ“, i.e. He does not reckon provision with him in this world in proportion to deeds; but provision in the Hereafter is in proportion to deeds, together with what Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, bestows out of His bounty.

zajjaj:284-284.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾: its meaning is: He is their Creator.
﴿وَإنْ تُبْدُوا ما في أنْفُسِكم أوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحاسِبْكم بِهِ اللَّهُ﴾: its meaning is: whether you act upon it openly or keep it secret, Allah will call you to account for it. It has been said that this is abrogated; it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: ”«تُجَوِّزَ لِهَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ عَنْ نِسْيانِها، وما حَدَّثَتْ بِهِ أنْفُسَها»“ (This community has been pardoned for its forgetting and for what its souls whisper to it).

zajjaj:285-285.t:
When Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — had mentioned the obligation of prayer and zakat, divorce, menstruation, the oath of abstention (al-īlāʾ), jihad, the stories of the prophets, debt and usury, He sealed the sura with mention of His magnification, and mention of His Prophet ﷺ and the believers affirming the truth of all of that, saying: ﴿آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْهِ مِن رَبِّهِ والمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, i.e. the Messenger affirmed the truth of all these things whose mention has passed, and likewise the believers. ﴿كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ﴾, i.e. affirmed the truth of Allah, ﴿وَمَلائِكَتِهِ وكُتُبِهِ﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās read: ”وَكِتابِهِ“, and a group of the readers read it so. As for ”كُتُبٌ“, it is the plural of ”كِتابٌ“, like ”مِثالٌ“ and ”مُثُلٌ“, and ”حِمارٌ“ and ”حُمُرٌ“. It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās about his reading ”وَكِتابِهِ“, and he said: ”كِتابٌ“ is more than ”كُتُبٌ“ — he took it as a generic noun (ism al-jins), as you say: ”كَثُرَ الدِّرْهَمُ في أيْدِي النّاسِ“ (the dirham has become plentiful in people's hands).

The meaning of ﴿لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أحَدٍ مِن رُسُلِهِ﴾ is: we do not do as the People of the Book before us did, who believed in some of the messengers and disbelieved in some, like the Jews' disbelief in Jesus and the Christians' disbelief in others besides him.
